source: Kuali Archive Enhancements and Requirements, Security Requirements tab
enforcementState: Record-level authorization is switched OFF in every environment, including the development website. Every gate described below is present in code and inert. Nothing on this page describes access control that is currently running.
recommendationStatus: The business decisions listed were approved on 2026-10-26. Implementation status is reported separately from them: an approved decision is not working software, and a passing test is not a released or verified one.
decisionsApproved: PAFO Administrator is a department user restricted to assigned departments, not a Central user.
“IO number” means the SAP account number.
Research Staff contact access extends to the entire Award family.
ARCHIVE_ADMIN may grant and revoke permissions.
Holding ARCHIVE_ADMIN does not by itself grant access to archive records.
An authenticated BU user with no assigned archive permissions receives Access Not Provisioned.
Dashboard statistics reflect only the records the user is authorised to see.
Central Users may see archive-wide statistics.
Unauthorised Award hierarchy relatives are omitted entirely, never shown as stubs.

moduleProgress.name: Authentication
moduleProgress.detail: BU Shibboleth with Duo, through Cognito SAML federation.

moduleProgress.name: Authorization engine
moduleProgress.detail: Policy, scope resolution, SQL predicate builder, evaluator, identity links, grants and the administrative service.
moduleProgress.evidence: PR #56, merged and deployed, inert while enforcement is off

moduleProgress.name: Award authorization
moduleProgress.detail: All 45 Award endpoints gated; scoped search, counts, exports, hierarchy and attachments.
moduleProgress.evidence: PR #62 - open and in draft, NOT merged

moduleProgress.name: Proposal authorization
moduleProgress.detail: The SQL predicate builder already supports Proposal; nothing is wired to it.

moduleProgress.name: Negotiation authorization
moduleProgress.detail: No approved record rule. Negotiation has no unit column, so department scoping cannot apply as written.

moduleProgress.name: IRB authorization
moduleProgress.detail: No approved record rule. IRB is a separate domain from the Proposal-Award chain.

moduleProgress.name: Enforcement
moduleProgress.detail: app.authorization.enforcement-enabled is unset everywhere and defaults to false. Every gate is inert.

requirements.requirement: Central users shall have unrestricted access to all system objects and functionality provided by the system.
requirements.audience: PAFO and OSP Administrators, and the Subaward, Contracting, Industry, Foundation Relations and Research Development teams.
requirements.acceptance: Verify a Central User can access all system objects and functionality.
requirements.businessRule: Central Users have unrestricted archive read access and may see archive-wide statistics. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: A Central scope renders no SQL predicate, so Central sees every record and archive-wide dashboard totals. Covered by decision3_centralSeesArchiveWideTotals and centralSeesEverythingIncludingRecordsWithNoUnitOrContact.
requirements.blockers: Membership cannot be derived: five of the seven Central teams named in the source document are not Kuali user roles, so Central membership has to be granted and maintained by hand. No administrative surface exists to do that yet.
requirements.decisions: Who administers Central grants, and whether granting Central access needs a second approver.
requirements.conflict: Five of the seven listed Central teams are not Kuali user roles, so Central membership cannot be derived from record contacts.

requirements.requirement: Department users shall have access to all system objects associated with their assigned department(s).
requirements.acceptance: Verify a Department User can access all objects within their assigned department and cannot access objects from unassigned departments.
requirements.businessRule: Department users see their assigned department and its authorised descendant units. PAFO Administrator is treated as a department user restricted to assigned departments, NOT as Central. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: Lead-unit matching with descendant expansion only where both the policy and the grant allow it. Covered by decision4_departmentTotalsDescribeOnlyTheirOwnRecords, departmentScopeReturnsOnlyItsOwnUnitAndTheCountAgrees, parentUnitWithDescendantsReachesTheChildUnit and parentUnitWithoutDescendantsReachesNothing.
requirements.blockers: Award only. Proposal, Negotiation, Subaward and IRB are not wired, and Negotiation has no unit column at all.

requirements.requirement: Research staff shall have access only to system objects on which they are directly listed as a contact.
requirements.accessScope: Objects directly assigned to the user
requirements.audience: PD/PI Contact, PD/PI Multiple and Co-Investigator.
requirements.acceptance: Verify Research Staff can access assigned objects and cannot access unassigned objects.
requirements.businessRule: Approved contact access extends to the entire Award family, not only the version a person is listed on. Access requires an approved contact role; being named on a record with any other role grants nothing. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: Contact matching against archived business data, restricted to approved role codes. Covered by contactScopeReachesTheAwardTheyAreListedOn, contactScopeIgnoresAListingWhoseRoleIsNotApproved and aPersonWhoIsNotAContactAnywhereSeesNothing.
requirements.blockers: Historical contact data is not evidence of current employment. A person listed on an archived record keeps that listing forever, so grants derived from it need periodic review that does not exist yet.

requirements.group: Other Authorized Viewers / SAP Account Access
requirements.requirement: Other authorized users shall have access only to specifically authorized system objects identified by IO number.
requirements.audience: Users authorised for named records only, typically to help a department with one task.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Authorized Viewer can access only the specifically authorized IO number(s).
requirements.businessRule: “IO number” means the SAP account number, and access granted that way is version-scoped. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: No automated coverage yet. The resolver and the SQL clause exist; no test drives an end-to-end SAP-account grant.
requirements.blockers: Implemented but untested. AwardAccountNumberIoResolver and the IO clause in the scope builder exist from Phase 1, and the terminology is now settled, but nothing exercises them and no grant of this kind has been created.
requirements.evidence: PR #56 (merged into main) for the resolver; PR #62 (open, draft - not merged) for the scope clause

requirements.requirement: The system shall support adding a user's access at both the role level and the specific IO number level based on the user's authorized role, department assignment, object assignment, or specific IO authorization.
requirements.audience: Whoever administers access for the archive.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Administrator can add access by assigning a role and/or specific IO number(s).
requirements.businessRule: ARCHIVE_ADMIN may grant and revoke permissions. Holding ARCHIVE_ADMIN does NOT by itself grant access to archive records. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: ArchiveAdminServiceTest and ArchiveAdminConcurrencyIntegrationTest cover granting, revoking, the last-administrator guard and concurrent membership changes against a real database.
requirements.blockers: No API surface and no user interface: the service exists and is tested, but nothing exposes it, so no administrator can actually grant anything yet. No bootstrap administrator has been created, deliberately.

requirements.requirement: The system shall support removing a user's access at both the role level and the specific IO number level when the user's role, department assignment, object assignment, or authorization changes.
requirements.audience: Whoever administers access for the archive.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Administrator can remove a role and/or specific IO access and that access is revoked.
requirements.businessRule: ARCHIVE_ADMIN may revoke permissions, and revocation takes effect on the caller's next request with no cache to clear. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: Covered by ArchiveAdminServiceTest, and by revokingAGrantTakesEffectOnTheNextRequestWithNoCacheToClear, which proves the scope is rebuilt per request rather than memoised.
requirements.blockers: Same as SEC-005: no API surface. The administrative service is merged (#56); the proof that revocation takes effect immediately is in #62, which is still an open draft. Also unresolved - nothing detects that a person's Kuali role or department assignment has changed upstream, so a grant stays active until someone revokes it by hand.
requirements.evidence: PR #56 (merged into main) and PR #62 (open, draft - not merged)
requirements.decisions: How a change of employment or department upstream becomes a revocation here.

requirements.requirement: The system shall enforce access restrictions when a user attempts to access a system object for which they are not authorized.
requirements.acceptance: Attempt to access an unauthorized object and verify that access is denied
requirements.businessRule: Enforcement is server-side and fails closed. An authenticated BU user with no assigned archive permissions receives Access Not Provisioned and no research data. Unauthorised Award hierarchy relatives are omitted entirely, not shown as stubs. Approved 2026-10-26.
requirements.tests: 31 integration cases against a disposable PostgreSQL: scoped search and counts, direct-URL denial returning 404 rather than 403, Access Not Provisioned, family completeness, hierarchy omission, cross-module refusal and the enforcement-disabled baseline.
requirements.blockers: Award only. Proposal, Negotiation, Subaward and IRB endpoints are unwired and can carry Award identifiers, so enabling enforcement today would protect Awards while other modules disclose them. Enforcement must stay OFF until those are covered.

requirements.requirement: The system shall maintain an auditable record of all archive activity, including the user, date and time, and action performed, to support security investigations when necessary.
requirements.acceptance: No test case was supplied in the source document. Acceptance cannot be agreed until the scope question below is answered.
requirements.businessRule: NOT RESOLVED. An earlier decision against routine audit logging has not been reconciled with this requirement, which asks for an auditable record of all archive activity.
requirements.tests: AuthorizationSchemaAndAuditIntegrationTest covers the administrative audit table and its transaction behaviour. There is no coverage of read logging, because there is no read logging.
requirements.blockers: The open question is scope: “all archive activity” in a read-only archive means logging reads, which is the expensive interpretation and the one previously decided against. Administrative actions are audited; reads are not. This needs Anthony's answer before it can be called done.
requirements.decisions: Does “all archive activity” include reads? The earlier decision said no; the requirement as written says yes. These have not been reconciled.
requirements.conflict: An earlier project decision against routine audit logging conflicts with this requirement as written. Recorded as unresolved rather than closed.

requirements.requirement: The system shall provide the archive in a read-only state to prevent historical records from being modified, updated, or deleted.
requirements.acceptance: No test case was supplied in the source document. Proposed: evidence that no write path reaches the archive schema, plus the database grants the API role holds.
requirements.businessRule: No decision recorded. The archive is read-only by charter and architecture, but no demonstrable control has been stated.
requirements.tests: No test asserts the absence of a write path. The claim currently rests on design and code review, not on evidence.
requirements.blockers: Needs a demonstrable control rather than an assertion: a test proving no write path reaches the archive schema, and a statement of what grants the API's database role actually holds. Both are straightforward; neither exists.
requirements.evidence: Architecture and charter; no dedicated evidence yet
requirements.decisions: What counts as sufficient proof of read-only: a test, a database grant listing, or both.
